rulings.sentence: **Framework (`blocksuite/framework/`)** has four core packages: ... **Affine feature layer (`blocksuite/affine/`)** builds on the framework.
rulings.reason: Gives the two groups with their contents and that the components build on the framework, which states the one-way dependency.

rulings.sentence: `store`: the Yjs-backed document model, meaning blocks, schemas and transactions.
rulings.reason: Identifies `store` as the data layer built on the Yjs CRDT; the collaboration and undo/redo it brings follow from Yjs rather than being a separate claim.

rulings.sentence: `std`: the runtime for block views, selection, commands and the canvas (gfx).
rulings.reason: Has block views, selection and commands, but leaves out both UI event handling and clipboard, so the description is partial.

rulings.sentence: **`widgets/`**: UI overlays such as the drag handle, slash menu, toolbar, keyboard toolbar, linked-doc, remote-selection, and the edgeless toolbar and zoom toolbar. ... **`fragments/`**: side panels such as outline, frame-panel, adapter-panel and doc-title.
rulings.reason: Blocks, widgets and fragments are covered with examples, but editors are not listed as a component type.

rulings.sentence: Blocks, widgets, inlines and gfx elements each ship their own store and view extensions. `std` collects those extensions into an editor.
rulings.reason: Conveys that an editor is a collection of block and widget registrations, but not `EditorHost`, page and edgeless as two views of one document, or the shared root model.

rulings.sentence: Its children are one `affine:surface` block and the `affine:note` blocks. ... The `affine:surface` block has one prop, `elements`.
rulings.reason: The surface block is a child of the root and holds the canvas elements and the canvas blocks, i.e. it is the container for the graphical content; "first child" is a detail.

rulings.sentence: Notes hold the page-mode content (paragraphs, lists and so on). In edgeless mode they appear as movable cards.
rulings.reason: Flowing content sits in note blocks among the root's children, shown as the document in page mode and placed as separate movable cards in edgeless mode.

rulings.sentence: A `group` element has a `children` Y.Map of `childId → true`, plus a `title` Y.Text (`elements/group/group.ts`). ... A `frame` is a block. It keeps `childElementIds: Record<id, boolean>` and its own `xywh` and `index` (`frame-model.ts`).
rulings.reason: Groups store child ids, but frames appear only as blocks with child ids and a position, not as areas that carry their contents by geometry, and group bounds and nesting are missing.

rulings.sentence: Headless plugins are the exception. ... **Theia plugins** import `@theia/plugin` in Node. ... **VS Code extensions** import `vscode`. ... This is why Theia's API is meant to be a superset of VS Code's.
rulings.reason: The three kinds and the superset relation are there, but not that plugins can be installed and removed at runtime, unlike Theia extensions built into the application.

rulings.sentence: **`MutableDisposable`** holds a single value. Assigning a new one disposes the old.
rulings.reason: Gives the replace-disposes-old behaviour, but not that disposing the holder disposes the current value, and not the use case (something a method creates on each run, where `this._register(...)` would pile up listeners).

rulings.sentence: The `vscode-api-tests` extension and other extension tests also run in this group. ... Run them with `scripts/test-integration.sh` (or `.bat`).
rulings.reason: The extension and API tests run by `test-integration.sh` are stated, but not that it launches a full VS Code with `--extensionDevelopmentPath`, nor that `--suite` picks which ones.

rulings.sentence: `props: (internal) => ({...})` gives the default props. It uses helpers such as `internal.Text()`.
rulings.reason: Names the `internal` helpers and `internal.Text()`, but not that they create Yjs-backed values (a Y.Text for the block's rich text), which is what the point is about.

rulings.sentence: `StoreExtensionProvider` is in `store.ts`. In `setup(context)` it calls `context.register(...)` with the schema extension and the adapter extensions (`ParagraphBlockAdapterExtensions`). ... Its `setup(context, options)` registers `FlavourExtension('affine:paragraph')`, `BlockViewExtension`, keymap extensions, a block config extension and markdown extensions. ... An editor or workspace then adds these providers to its store and view extension lists.
rulings.reason: Both providers are named with the right data and UI split, and the editor collecting the providers into store and view extension lists is described; only the two manager class names are missing.

rulings.sentence: `defineBlockSchema({ flavour, metadata, toModel })` comes from `@blocksuite/store`. ... The flavour is a namespaced string such as `'affine:divider'`. ... `metadata` holds `version`, `role` (for example `'content'`) and the allowed `children`.
rulings.reason: The flavour and the metadata with version and role are right, but the schema's `props`, one of its three parts, are never mentioned.

rulings.sentence: Registration happens as a side effect of importing the module, for example from `workbench.common.main.ts` and the other `*.main.ts` files.
rulings.reason: A side effect of importing the module is module-scope code, and importing it from the main entry files means it runs at startup.
